answer.evidence: The width profile at the top is 8, 12, then 14 held for rows 2-7, so the cap is rounded only at its upper edge and ends flat. It does not narrow again below the widest rows, so it is a hat-like cap rather than an ellipse plate. It still shows a light top surface in rows 1-5 with a hollow oval mark. A teal front band in rows 6-7 darkens like an eave shadow beneath it. The cap overhangs the 10-wide sign box (rows 8-16) and the 11-wide shaft (rows 17-25). The front face runs from row 8 to row 29, including the number panel, the shaft and a wider base in rows 26-29. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small bollard-style sign: a pale cap with a dark band, a teal-grey body and a dark base. It has about 4 visible lightness steps on the body and 3-4 on the cap. Its 12 visible tones per tile match kiosk-a (12) and exceed bus-shelter-a (6), though it sits below vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 15%, higher than kiosk and vending (0%) and above bus-shelter (9%), so some of the pole body is a plain fill. The measured neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, so the outline carries a tint of the neighbouring material, as in the references. Texture is limited to a few highlight and shadow dots on the pole and a simple sign face with no grain. It is not thinner than the shipped bus-shelter and is comparable to the kiosk, but it is a little flatter and simpler than the kiosk and vending references.
